drhp.business: Om Freight Forwarders operates in the logistics and allied services business as Clearing and Forwarding agents, Custom House Agents, Common Carriers Freight Booking Agents and Cargo Booking Agents in air and sea transport, and in the business of warehousing. It undertakes CHA & clearance, freight booking, shipping, transportation, vessel agency and stevedoring services, and is expanding into custom bonded and general/public warehousing to extend from 3PL into 4PL solutions.
drhp.end_markets: Domestic and international (EXIM) trade|Over 700 national and international destinations|Global presence across 5 continents
drhp.expansion: The Company commenced a new warehouse during the year, an important milestone in its infrastructure expansion strategy that strengthens integrated logistics and warehousing capabilities and enables extension of 4PL solutions alongside existing 3PL services. Subsequent to the financial year-end, the Company acquired approximately 1,98,000 sq. ft. of open and closed land for warehousing and allied logistics operations, taking its aggregate open and closed land and warehousing footprint (owned and leased, operational and vacant) to approximately 4,48,000 sq. ft. as on date. The Company acquired land parcels during the year as part of a long-term infrastructure expansion strategy, with proposed development of warehousing and logistics infrastructure on these parcels expected to enhance operational capabilities and service coverage. Going forward, the Company will continue to expand its transportation and warehousing capabilities in a calibrated manner in line with business requirements and customer demand.

litigation.note: The Company filed a Suo-Moto application for adjudication under Section 454 of the Companies Act, 2013, relating to a default under Section 129 of the said Act, as disclosed in the Directors' Report (Voluntary Revision of Financial Statements).

drhp.mdna: The Company remains positive about the long-term prospects of the logistics and supply-chain industry, supported by continued growth of domestic and international trade, increasing outsourcing of logistics activities and development of India's logistics infrastructure.|Established capabilities in CHA and clearance, freight booking, shipping, transportation, vessel agency, stevedoring and allied logistics services, supported by its existing transportation fleet and warehousing facilities, provide a platform to serve evolving customer requirements.|During the year, the Company acquired land parcels as part of its long-term infrastructure expansion strategy, aimed at strengthening its logistics network and creating additional capacity for future business growth.|The proposed development of warehousing and logistics infrastructure on the acquired land parcels is expected to enhance operational capabilities, improve service coverage and provide greater flexibility in meeting customer requirements.|Profit margins were affected during the fourth quarter due to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, which caused significant fluctuations in rates quoted by agents and service providers; with easing of these conditions, the Company expects a gradual recovery in profit margins in coming quarters.|The Company remains cognisant of challenges from freight-rate volatility, geopolitical developments, fuel costs, regulatory changes and global trade uncertainties, and will continue to focus on operational efficiency and prudent risk management.

risks.note: Fluctuations in freight rates, fuel prices, port charges, transportation, warehousing and other operating costs may affect margins, particularly where increases cannot be fully passed on to customers.
risks.risk: Freight rate and operating cost volatility

risks.note: Changes in international trade policies, tariffs, geopolitical tensions, disruption of shipping routes and fluctuations in global trade volumes may affect cargo movement, freight rates, transit times and overall business volumes.

Operations involve coordination with shipping lines, transporters, ports and other third-party service providers; disruptions in their services, port congestion, capacity constraints or infrastructure-related interruptions may affect service delivery and operating costs.
risks.risk: Dependence on service providers and logistics infrastructure

risks.note: Transportation, cargo handling, loading and unloading activities involve risks of cargo loss or damage, accidents, delays and other operational incidents, which may result in claims, additional costs and reputational impact.

Operations are subject to various customs, EXIM, shipping, transportation, labour and other applicable laws and regulations; changes in requirements or non-compliance may result in additional costs, penalties or operational disruptions.

The logistics industry is highly competitive, including domestic and international logistics, freight forwarding, shipping and integrated supply-chain service providers; increased competition and pricing pressure may affect margins and market position.
Delays in collection or deterioration in the financial position of customers and other counterparties may affect working capital requirements and cash flows.

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Domestic and international (EXIM) trade
- Over 700 national and international destinations
- Global presence across 5 continents

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- The Company remains positive about the long-term prospects of the logistics and supply-chain industry, supported by continued growth of domestic and international trade, increasing outsourcing of logistics activities and development of India's logistics infrastructure.
- Established capabilities in CHA and clearance, freight booking, shipping, transportation, vessel agency, stevedoring and allied logistics services, supported by its existing transportation fleet and warehousing facilities, provide a platform to serve evolving customer requirements.
- During the year, the Company acquired land parcels as part of its long-term infrastructure expansion strategy, aimed at strengthening its logistics network and creating additional capacity for future business growth.
- The proposed development of warehousing and logistics infrastructure on the acquired land parcels is expected to enhance operational capabilities, improve service coverage and provide greater flexibility in meeting customer requirements.
- Profit margins were affected during the fourth quarter due to geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, which caused significant fluctuations in rates quoted by agents and service providers; with easing of these conditions, the Company expects a gradual recovery in profit margins in coming quarters.
- The Company remains cognisant of challenges from freight-rate volatility, geopolitical developments, fuel costs, regulatory changes and global trade uncertainties, and will continue to focus on operational efficiency and prudent risk management.

capex_expansion.title: Expansion (RHP)
capex_expansion.body: The Company commenced a new warehouse during the year, an important milestone in its infrastructure expansion strategy that strengthens integrated logistics and warehousing capabilities and enables extension of 4PL solutions alongside existing 3PL services. Subsequent to the financial year-end, the Company acquired approximately 1,98,000 sq. ft. of open and closed land for warehousing and allied logistics operations, taking its aggregate open and closed land and warehousing footprint (owned and leased, operational and vacant) to approximately 4,48,000 sq. ft. as on date. The Company acquired land parcels during the year as part of a long-term infrastructure expansion strategy, with proposed development of warehousing and logistics infrastructure on these parcels expected to enhance operational capabilities and service coverage. Going forward, the Company will continue to expand its transportation and warehousing capabilities in a calibrated manner in line with business requirements and customer demand.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- scale: More than 5 decades of domain expertise as a 3rd-generation international logistics, customs broker, freight forwarding and allied-services company — evidence: branches at major seaports, airports and ICDs in India (18 offices) and overseas offices, catering to over 700 national and international destinations
- integration: Ownership of a significant portion of its operating equipment gives greater operational control and flexibility — evidence: more than 50% of the equipment deployed for its operations is owned by the Company itself
- distribution: Expanding owned warehousing footprint alongside existing leased facilities supports long-term capacity and integrated 3PL/4PL service delivery — evidence: aggregate open and closed land and warehousing footprint of approximately 4,48,000 sq. ft. as on date, including a ~1,98,000 sq. ft. parcel acquired after year-end [planned]

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Fluctuations in freight rates, fuel prices, port charges, transportation, warehousing and other operating costs may affect margins, particularly where increases cannot be fully passed on to customers.
- Changes in international trade policies, tariffs, geopolitical tensions, disruption of shipping routes and fluctuations in global trade volumes may affect cargo movement, freight rates, transit times and overall business volumes.
- Operations involve coordination with shipping lines, transporters, ports and other third-party service providers; disruptions in their services, port congestion, capacity constraints or infrastructure-related interruptions may affect service delivery and operating costs.
- Transportation, cargo handling, loading and unloading activities involve risks of cargo loss or damage, accidents, delays and other operational incidents, which may result in claims, additional costs and reputational impact.
- Operations are subject to various customs, EXIM, shipping, transportation, labour and other applicable laws and regulations; changes in requirements or non-compliance may result in additional costs, penalties or operational disruptions.
- The logistics industry is highly competitive, including domestic and international logistics, freight forwarding, shipping and integrated supply-chain service providers; increased competition and pricing pressure may affect margins and market position.
- Delays in collection or deterioration in the financial position of customers and other counterparties may affect working capital requirements and cash flows.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue to expand transportation and warehousing capabilities in a calibrated manner, in line with business requirements and customer demand.
- Strengthen EXIM logistics and freight-related services while enhancing integrated 3PL and 4PL supply-chain solutions.
- Leverage technology, operational efficiencies and an integrated service model to provide comprehensive, efficient and reliable logistics solutions and improve customer engagement.
- Leverage existing infrastructure, operational capabilities and customer relationships to pursue opportunities in transportation, warehousing and integrated logistics services.
- Focus on undertaking quality projects with better long-term value instead of increasing business volume, to support sustainable growth and improve overall business quality.
